atom:entry.atom:summary:
Severity: CRITICAL / CVSS 9.3
Summary: Vasion Print (formerly PrinterLogic) Virtual Appliance Host and Application (VA and SaaS deployments) mount host configuration and secret material under /var/www/efs_storage into many Docker containers with overly-permissive filesystem permissions. Files such as secrets.env, GPG-encrypted blobs in .secrets, MySQL client keys, and application session files are accessible from multiple containers. An attacker who controls or reaches any container can read or modify these artifacts, leading to credential theft, RCE via Laravel APP_KEY, Portainer takeover, and full compromise.

atom:entry.atom:title: code-review-mcp-server: Command injection via unsanitized folderPath/baseBranch parameters
atom:entry.atom:summary:
Severity: HIGH
Summary: ### Impact `code-review-mcp-server` exposes MCP tools (`getLocalGitDiff`, `codeReview`, `createPR`, `getPRTemplate`) that accept `folderPath` and `baseBranch` string parameters. These caller-controlled values were interpolated directly into shell command strings executed via `child_process.execSync()`, which runs commands through `/bin/sh`. A crafted value such as `baseBranch = "main; <arbitrary command> #"` (or a `$(...)` command substitution, or a `folderPath` that breaks out of the surrounding quotes) results in **arbitrary command execution** on the host running the MCP server. ### Patches Fixed in **1.5.3**. Every `execSync()` call was replaced with `execFileSync()` using argument arrays, so inputs are passed directly to `git` / `gh` without going through a shell, eliminating the injection at its root. ### Workarounds None. Upgrade to `code-review-mcp-server@1.5.3` or later.
Suggested next step: Check whether affected package versions are present in your dependencies and review the maintainer's fix guidance.
Original advisory: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-jq3q-62jc-fqq9
Watchlist match only. Local exposure has not been assessed.
